content_voiceover: This slide summarizes Taiwan's National Health Insurance reimbursement criteria for tisagenlecleucel, or Kymriah. It is covered for patients with refractory disease, relapse after transplant, or second or later relapse of B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, provided several conditions are met. First, the patient must be twenty five years of age or younger. Second, the patient must have relapsed after second line standard treatment regimens, such as TPOG protocol, GRAALL, or Hyper-CVAD, or after hematopoietic stem cell transplant, or alternatively must be confirmed by two specialists trained in hematology and stem cell transplantation as unable to undergo transplant due to refractory disease. Third, if the patient has already relapsed after allogeneic transplant, they may receive Kymriah regardless of whether their disease status is complete remission, partial remission, or progressive disease. Fourth, the patient must have an expected survival of at least three months and must fully meet a set of organ function criteria, including ECOG performance status less than two documented on at least three occasions, adequate renal function with eGFR at least sixty or creatinine no more than one point five times the upper limit of normal, adequate liver function with ALT no more than five times upper limit of normal and bilirubin under two point five, adequate cardiac function with left ventricular ejection fraction over fifty percent and no pericardial effusion or major cardiac disease in the past year, and adequate pulmonary function with oxygen saturation above ninety two percent on room air documented at least twice.
keypoints: Taiwan NHI covers Kymriah for refractory, post-transplant relapse, or second or later relapse B-ALL
Age twenty five or younger, and failed second line therapy or transplant, or confirmed transplant ineligible
Post allogeneic transplant relapse patients eligible regardless of disease status at treatment
Requires expected survival over three months plus adequate ECOG, renal, hepatic, cardiac, and pulmonary function
keypoint_voiceover: Know the general framework of Taiwan's NHI Kymriah criteria. It covers young patients, twenty five or under, with refractory or relapsed B-ALL after standard therapy or transplant, and requires adequate organ function and performance status to ensure the patient can safely tolerate CAR T cell therapy.
